title: Placed Consumer Accounts: One Account per Placed Debt and Duplicate Placements
content:
Clause of the client placement terms for **Placed Consumer Accounts**, on how placed debts map to accounts and when a placement duplicates one already open.

## Clause

1. A consumer may hold any number of placed accounts at Ridgeline, one for each debt a client places. There is no limit on the number of placed accounts one consumer may hold.
2. Debts from different clients, different placement agreements or different client account numbers are never merged into one account.
3. A placement is accepted only when no other placed account carrying the same client account number under the same placement agreement is in a non-terminal status.
4. The terminal statuses are paid in full, settled in full and returned to client. The non-terminal statuses are placed, validation period, active, arranged, dispute hold and hardship hold.
5. A client that re-places a debt whose earlier placement is terminal opens a new placed account with its own placement date, and the earlier account and its history stay unchanged.

## Basis of the duplicate test

The test in clause 3 is made on Ridgeline's own records before the placement is accepted: the placement agreement, the client account number and the status of any existing placed account. The object compared is the pair "placement agreement plus client account number"; the same client account number under a different placement agreement is a different object and never blocks the placement.

## Points of judgement

| Existing placed account with the same client account number under the same placement agreement | Placement accepted |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| One, in status active (or any other non-terminal status) | No |
| One, in status paid in full, settled in full or returned to client | Yes, as a new placed account with its own placement date |

*Hypothetical cases.*

- A client places a bank-card debt for a consumer who already has two medical accounts at Ridgeline from a hospital client. Each debt is its own account; the new debt opens a third account and nothing is merged.
- A client re-places a debt whose earlier placed account was returned to client. The re-placement opens a new account; the returned account keeps its balance, dates and case history exactly as they were.
- A client sends the same client account number under the same placement agreement while the earlier placed account is in dispute hold. Dispute hold is a non-terminal status, so the placement is not accepted.
